sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:1
items.html: The expansion of lights is along the lines of the above, in the words of the Rav (Part 3, Chapter 1, item 3), that Ein Sof expanded to make vessels, through the coupling by striking and the raising of reflected light, see there. And he says here, that immediately in the world of Adam Kadmon, there began to be extended from it a great expansion of lights, through that same coupling by striking, to the point of emanating twenty-five Partzufim in that world, and these twenty-five Partzufim of AK "will be the aspects of roots and sources for the Atzilut that will be emanated afterward." That is, for the twenty-five Partzufim that will be emanated in the world of Atzilut, as will be written before us. And so the Rav writes, "a great expansion of lights, to become the aspects of roots and sources for the Atzilut." And as he continues to explain this before us.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:2
items.html:
Know, that this reflected light that is returned to its place through the coupling by striking, as above in the words of the Rav (Part 3, Chapter 1, item 3), is called "the breath that goes out from the Partzuf," or the wind that goes out from the Partzuf, meaning, that it cannot be clothed in it, because of the force of restraint in the screen there, and therefore it is forced to go out of it and return to its place (see Inner Observation, Part 2, item 2).
You also need to know, that just as there are five discernments that include the whole of reality after the restriction, called: AK, Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Assiyah — which are five degrees of stature, one below the other, from the stature of Keter to Malchut, whose cause is the refinement of the screen (see Inner Observation, Part 2, item 17), for because the screen of phase four that served in AK was refined, and remained at the coarseness of phase three, ten Sefirot came out and were renewed at the stature of Hochma, called Atzilut. And because after that, the screen of phase three was also refined and remained at the coarseness of phase two, new ten Sefirot came out and were born at the stature of Bina, called Beriah, and so on (as above in the words of the Rav, Part 3, Chapter 4, item 3, and in Ohr Pnimi, item 9), until the screen was refined of all its coarseness, and nothing remained in it but its root, at which point there is no striking there, and no stature of reflected light there at all, and because of this, ten Sefirot come out here in the aspect of Malchut alone, which are called the world of Assiyah. And for exactly the same reason and cause explained regarding the four general degrees of stature, which are AK and ABYA, it is likewise necessary that five stature-degrees of ten Sefirot come out in each and every world of them, called five Partzufim: Arich Anpin, Abba, Ima, Zeir Anpin, Nukva. And moreover, in each and every one of these Partzufim, it is likewise necessary that five stature-degrees of ten Sefirot come out, one below the other, down to Malchut, called: Galgalta, Einayim, Ozen, Hotem, Peh, or KHB, ZA, and Malchut, or NRNHY. And this matter will be explained in full in Inner Observation here, for it cannot be detailed here at length.
And so the Rav writes, "according to the measure of the limb so will be its fineness, etc." Explanation: the vessel in which the light designated for it is clothed is called a "limb," and the measure of the fineness or coarseness of the limb is gauged by the coarseness of the screen serving there.
And therefore, the place of service of the screen of phase two is called a "fine limb," "and the wind that goes out from it is very fine," meaning, the reflected light that ascends and is returned from that vessel is very fine, because it does not reach Keter or Hochma, but only Bina, and therefore those ten Sefirot, their stature reaches only to Bina, as explained above.
And this is what he said, "and after it in rank is the limb of the nose, for from it comes a more perceptible wind than what comes from the ear": for the place of service of the screen of phase three is called nose, whose "wind that goes out from it," meaning, the reflected light returned backward and going out from that vessel, its measure is greater, and it therefore reaches to Hochma, and therefore the ten Sefirot of the nose, their stature reaches to Hochma. And so he said, "and after it in rank is the limb of the mouth, for from it comes a breath and wind stronger than all of them": for the place of service of the screen of phase four is called "mouth," whose breath that goes out from it, which is the secret of the reflected light departing from it and rising upward, is stronger than all of them, because its measure is full, reaching to Keter, and therefore those ten Sefirot have the stature of Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:3
items.html:
And although the ten Sefirot that come from the coupling by striking in the screen of the mouth have the stature of Keter, which is the light of Yechida, and from the nose the stature of Hochma, which is the light of Chaya, and so on, nevertheless, the order of the clothing of the lights in them is not so, but rather in reverse order, for the more important light is clothed in the more refined vessel, in such a way that the light of Yechida is clothed only in the most refined of all, called Keter, or Galgalta. And the light of Chaya is clothed only in the vessel of Hochma, which is phase one, called Einayim. And the light of Neshama is clothed only in the vessel of Bina, which is phase two, called Ozen. And the light of Ruach is clothed only in the vessel of ZA, that is, phase three, called Hotem. And the light of Nefesh is clothed in the vessel of Malchut, which is phase four, called Peh.
And this is the rule, "every giver must have the coarser discernment, and every receiver must receive with the more refined thing." Explanation: the extension of the upper light to bestow upon the lower one requires that the lower one have the aspect of screen and vessel that is the coarsest, as above, for the coarser the screen, the greater the measure of reflected light that departs from it, and it is thus found that it reaches to a higher stature, for therefore, if the lower one has only the screen of phase three, it lacks the stature of Yechida, and has only the stature of Chaya, etc. However, the reception of the lower one is always with the more refined thing, meaning, that the light bestowed upon it is clothed only in the more refined discernment, and every more important light needs the more refined vessel. And I have already explained this matter at great length, in Inner Observation, Part 2 (see item 87, entry "and this is").

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:4
items.html: This teaches us, that the force of the coarseness of the screen is discerned by us only in its expansion from above downward (as written above in Ohr Pnimi, Part 3, Chapter 4, item 50), for after every coupling by striking, in which the reflected light ascends and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light from Malchut upward, to the aspect of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh and the roots of the four discernments, after this, it returns and descends and expands from Malchut downward at that same measure of stature that it has in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh from below upward, see there. Now the reflected light that ascends from below upward does not carry with it any coarseness there, as written there, but rather it is those ten Sefirot that expand from above downward that are entirely limited by the measure and boundary of the stature of the screen, since the screen is the whole root of them.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:5
items.html:
Explanation: the coarseness of phase one, called Einayim, is very slight, and this is for the reason explained in Ohr Pnimi (page 5, entry "and the reason"), that the matter of the aforementioned coarseness means the thing of the will to receive that is in every emanated being, in which it differs from the upper light, which has no will to receive, see there. And therefore, phase one is found to have coarseness that is slight, since it is drawn to it from the force of the upper one, for the will to bestow that is in the upper one is a law imposed on the lower one, that it should have a will to receive its bestowal, and therefore this is not considered in the lower one as a change of form and coarseness, until the aspect of will is aroused in it from the force of its own arousal, which is phase two (see entry "now").
And therefore, coupling by striking does not apply to the light of Einayim, which is phase one, because the reflected light, which is the breath that goes out from phase one, remains in its place, meaning that it does not depart from it in the secret of reflected light. And so the Rav writes, "but the eyes are not so, for their breath itself remains in its place," as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:6
items.html: Meaning, the light of Hochma has no vessel to be clothed in, because there is no reflected light, which is the secret of a vessel, in the eyes, as above in the adjacent discussion, and therefore the light of Hochma remains outside, and shines from afar without clothing. And this light is called the light of Chaya, or Neshama LeNeshama.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:7
items.html:
You need to know, that the matter of the restriction and the screen that was made applies only to the light of Hochma alone, and not to the light of Chassadim (see Inner Observation, Part 1, item 6). And therefore, the matter of the expansion of Ein Sof to make vessels (mentioned above in the words of the Rav, Part 3, Chapter 1, item 3) through the coupling by striking in the screen — this coupling by striking is only from the aspect of the light of Hochma, called sight and looking, for only that light is not received in phase four because of the screen and the restriction, whereas phase two and Bina, which are the secret of the light of Chassadim, have no aspect of screen holding them back.
And so the Rav writes, "therefore in this looking alone was there the power to create and make the vessels, and not from the breath itself, unlike in AHP." That is, as explained, that only the light of the eyes, called looking, upon which was the restriction, therefore has striking and reflected light, which are the secret of the vessels, unlike in AHP, whose primary light is the light of Chassadim, as above, so that on their part there is no striking at all, and whatever coupling by striking does operate even in AHP is only from the force of the light of Hochma shining in them, which is called the looking of the eyes in AHP, for because of the illumination of the light of Hochma in them, the screen is found to hold back even the lights in AHP as well, and remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:8
items.html:
That is, from the breaths that expand from them downward, as above in the adjacent Ohr Pnimi of this chapter, item 4, see there, which is the reflected light descending from above downward.
Similar to what is written concerning the Sefira of Malchut in Inner Observation (Part 2, item 109, entry "and Netzach"), that phase four, called here mouth, does not receive anything at all from direct light, because of the screen in it, but rather, after the reflected light is raised from it upward, this reflected light returns and descends from the screen downward and expands Malchut into ten Sefirot of her own, within her (as above, Part 3, Chapter 2, item 3), and receives within them the entire measure of stature of the ten Sefirot that the reflected light clothed from Malchut upward, see there.
And in exactly the same way, the vessels of ear and nose receive nothing at all from the breath, that is, the reflected light ascending from them upward, for since the screen is refined from phase four to phase three, it is discerned that Malchut has risen to the place of ZA, that is, to the nose, so that because of this the screen holds back the vessel of the nose, so that it receives nothing at all from direct light, and therefore returns that light upward, which is called coupling by striking in phase three, as above. So then, the vessel of the nose receives nothing at all from the direct light, since it departs from it, but only afterward, after the reflected light expands and descends from the nose downward, as above regarding Malchut in the place of phase four, that is, the mouth. And likewise the vessel called ear receives nothing at all from direct light for the same reason, but only through the reflected light descending from the ear downward, in the same way as above.
And so the Rav writes, "unlike in AHP, which are lower, it was necessary that their very breath itself expand." That is, after the breath itself, that is, the reflected light, descends and expands from above downward, it then expands into ten Sefirot and becomes vessels to receive the light. And this is what he said, "and no reality at all was made from them except by the force of the breath itself." That is, by the force of their reflected light, called breath, which turns and descends from above downward, in the manner explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:9
items.html: As written above, that phase one does not raise a breath, which is reflected light, because its coarseness is very slight, and it does not make a coupling by striking. And so the Rav writes, "there was no breath at all, only looking alone." That is, there is no reflected light there, but only direct light alone, which is the light of Hochma, called "looking," as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:10
items.html: That is, from the aspect of the eye itself no vessel at all is made, because there is no breath there, but rather the aspect of its striking is what makes the vessels, in the ear, nose, and mouth: for were it not for the light of Hochma, called looking, there would be no coupling by striking there, as above, and there would be no vessel at all even in AHP, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:11:11
items.html: For the breath of phase four that expands from the mouth downward becomes a vessel for Nefesh, and the breath of phase three for Ruach, and the breath of phase two for Neshama, as above. And remember here the inverse relationship between the bestowal of the light and the reception of the light, as written in Ohr Pnimi (above, this chapter, item 3).
